metadata.hardware_requirements: a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Video data from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices, serving as inputs for the DRL method. Three consecutive frames are used as observation input for each decision time step.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Data serving as the basis for a series of simulation experiments conducted to evaluate the proposed DRL approach.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used for calibrating simulation parameters related to driving behaviors. It includes 10-min traffic volumes in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations and form position matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y) are extracted from raw video frames. These locations, along with signal states, are used to form position matrices (m_t).

nodes_process.source_quote: For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: Position matrices are down-sampled to reduce input dimensions while maintaining sufficient information about vehicle positions.

nodes_process.node_name: Stack matrices for traffic state representation
nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_{t-(N-1)},...,m_t}.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive N down-sampled position matrices are stacked to represent the traffic state s_t, capturing vehicle dynamics.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network architecture is defined with three CNN layers and two FC output layers (one for speed+queue, one for Q function), revised from Mnih et al. [30]. It has about 2 million weights.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools+params stated based on Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = u*v_t + w*q_t, u > 0, w < 0,
nodes_process.description: The reward r_t function is defined for the DRL agent, based on the average speed in the merging area (v_t) and the average queue length at the on-ramp (q_t), weighted by parameters mu (u) and omega (w).

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The ramp meter takes new action with the e-greedy strategy
nodes_process.description: The DRL model is trained using a Q-network, experience replay, a target network, and a multitask learning strategy. The Adam optimizer minimizes a total loss function L(w_i) = L_1(w_i) + lambda*L_2(w_i), selecting actions with an epsilon-greedy strategy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/6 tools named, 8/9 params stated (discount_factor_gamma missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO. The road network, simulation time, speed limits, and driving behavior parameters are configured based on empirical data from Qingdao and Huangdao.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/1 tool named, 4/5 params stated (driving_behavior_parameters values missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: Implements the PI-ALINEA ramp metering method, which adjusts the red phase length based on a proportional-integral control law, using downstream occupancies.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool named, all params stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate DRL and baseline methods in simulation
nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: The trained DRL model is evaluated and compared against a no-control scenario and the PI-ALINEA method within the SUMO simulation environment. The evaluation consists of 20 simulation experiments measuring travel times, queue lengths, and traffic flows.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, 1/2 params stated (random_seeds mentioned but not specified).

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 6 presents the 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Bar chart showing 10-minute traffic volumes for mainline and on-ramp between 7:50 a.m. and 8:50 a.m., used as input for simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Empirical data is presented visually; raw source data is not provided for direct verification.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times (in seconds) for 20 simulation experiments under three scenarios: No controls, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL, with percentage differences.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation outcomes are presented numerically. Upstream simulation outputs not directly traceable (no raw data/code).

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Plots showing the convergence of episode reward and mean travel time over 1.0e6 frames during the deep Q-learning training process.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plots show training metrics. Algorithm details available, but code/exact setup (seeds) not provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series plot of vehicle travel times (min) in the mainline from 8:00 to 9:00 for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios, showing quartiles.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualizes simulation results, consistent with Table 2. Underlying simulation outputs not directly traceable.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency of the ramp metering and the better performance of the proposed method.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing the temporal-spatial distribution of mean speeds (m/s) along the mainline over time for (a) no-control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation outputs, which are not directly accessible. Methods are clearly described.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series plot of queue lengths (m) at the on-ramp from 8:00 to 9:00 for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios, showing quartiles.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualizes simulation results; underlying simulation outputs not directly traceable.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots showing the relationship between mean queue length (m) and red ratio (%) at the on-ramp for PI-ALINEA and Deep RL methods across simulations.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation outcomes, which are not directly accessible. Calculation of metrics is clear.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series plots showing queue length (m) and occupancy (%) over time for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL methods, including Pearson correlation coefficient (p).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation outcomes, which are not directly accessible. Calculation of metrics is clear.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plot showing downstream traffic volume (veh/h) over time (5-minute intervals) for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation outputs, which are not directly accessible. The summarization (box plot) is clear.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Box plot showing travel time (s) for baseline and 8 scenarios where information from different subareas is removed from the input data.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation outputs with perturbed inputs, which are not directly accessible. Perturbation details are somewhat general.
